# Mesh

> Mesh is a local proxy for LLM API traffic, for teams running their own agents on the Anthropic or OpenAI API: out of the box it makes three lossless changes to each request and records every saving in a hash-chained ledger on your own machine, so you can recompute the bill yourself.
> The fee is 1% of verified savings for the month, rounded down to the cent, and nothing else; no fee is due unless billing has been agreed in writing.

## What a fresh install does today
The three default changes are tool-schema compaction, exact-duplicate removal
and cache-prefix repair. They are lossless. On Mesh's own 30-request test
basket (LIVE, run 2026-10-26 on claude-sonnet-5-5, not a customer's traffic)
those three account for under half of the 18.2% of spend recorded; the rest
came from two levers that are off by default, a 5-minute Anthropic cache
stamp and a gate-approved cap on oversized tool results. A Claude Code user
gains little on the defaults. Mesh has no customers yet and has not been
measured on a customer's provider bill. No default-install percentage has
been published.

## Figures, each with its label, date and the levers it needed
LIVE means real API calls on a test basket Mesh wrote. SIMULATOR means
modelled on a harness at the providers' published prices; it is not a
measurement of anyone's bill. The "J stack" is tool-description trimming,
exact-duplicate removal, cache-prefix repair, a cap on oversized tool
results, stale-history compaction and an output cap; four of those six are
off in a fresh install.
- 18.2% of real spend: LIVE, run 2026-10-26, Mesh's own test basket; needed the three defaults plus a 5-minute cache stamp and a tool-result cap, both off by default. Spools: evals/live-exports-2026-10-26/.
- 37.9%, multi-turn Claude that places no cache breakpoints: SIMULATOR, verified 2026-10-22; needed the 5-minute Anthropic cache stamp alone, off by default.
- 57.3% lower simulated cost with 5 points lower clean-task quality: SIMULATOR, verified 2026-10-22; needed the J stack plus the cache stamp; fails the quality limit and is not a qualified saving.
- 57.7% net (64.3% ceiling), work that can wait: SIMULATOR, verified 2026-10-13; needed the J stack plus the provider's flex tier, not on by default.
- 45.5%, one-shot calls on a shared template: SIMULATOR, verified 2026-10-13; needed cache-prefix repair (on by default, carries most of it on a provider that caches automatically) plus description trimming, history compaction and an output cap (off by default).
- 72.8%, the same where the work can wait: SIMULATOR, verified 2026-10-13; needed the above plus the flex tier.
- 34.3%, sparse interactive agents: SIMULATOR, verified 2026-10-22; needed the J stack plus the 1-hour Anthropic cache stamp, off by default; may overstate on some models.
- 25.9–29.4%, busy interactive agents: SIMULATOR, verified 2026-10-13; needed the J stack; the three defaults alone move this simulated bill very little.
- 0–5%, stacks that are already optimised: SIMULATOR, fixture, 2026-10-11; nothing to switch on; the verdict is "do not pay us".

## Switching on more than the defaults
Nothing beyond the three default changes is automatic. Theo, the agent that
runs beside the proxy, can prove three lossy levers on a capture of the
user's own requests (tool-description trimming, stale-history compaction,
lower output effort) and propose them; the user accepts with
`mesh theo --accept <lever>`. The Anthropic cache stamp is added by hand to
the levers list in ~/.mesh/theo-policy.json as
{"lever":"cache-ttl-5m","class":"lossless"}, or set with
MESH_PROXY_CACHE_TTL=5m on the npm proxy. Details: start.html.

## Install
Open to everyone, no signup. Install with one command on macOS, Linux or WSL:
`curl -fsSL https://www.mesh-technology.com/install.sh | sh` (or
`npm install -g @harrym1707/mesh`; needs Node 22+). Then `mesh proxy` for any
app or agent: set the client's base URL to http://127.0.0.1:8787 (Anthropic)
or http://127.0.0.1:8787/v1 (OpenAI and compatibles) and keep your own key.
`mesh start` does the same for Claude Code. `mesh verify` recomputes the
invoice from the ledger the user holds, with no network calls. Without
installing: `npx -y -p @harrym1707/sdk mesh-proxy` runs the proxy alone, and
the invoice is recomputable with verifyLedgerChain and recomputeInvoice from
that package. Quote from an existing LiteLLM, Helicone or Langfuse export
without routing any traffic:
`npx -y -p @harrym1707/sdk mesh-quote your-export.jsonl --format litellm`.

## How a saving is verified
What was paid is the provider's own reported usage. What would have been paid
is worked out by Mesh from the tokens it removed, and is recorded as an
estimated baseline. Every request writes one hash-chained event; the invoice
is a pure function of those events. Prompts never leave the machine, and the
API key passes through to the provider and is never stored.
